text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike this morning in us-west-2: many cards reporting ECC corrections and rising Xid counts. Need quick decision on reserve strategy and auto-drain thresholds.

aj: Do you have the raw rates / timeframe? corrected vs uncorrected?

maria: Quick dump from Prom:
```
# corrected ECC per GPU per month (30d):
avg_over_time(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[30d]) / count(gpu_ecc_corrected_total) * 30
# fatal Xid per GPU per month:
avg_over_time(gpu_xid_fatal_total[30d]) / count(gpu_xid_fatal_total) * 30
```
Numbers I pulled: 30d window -> corrected ECC ≈ 1.2 events/gpu-month, fatal Xid ≈ 0.08/gpu-month. Last 7d shows a US-W spike: corrected ≈ 0.9, Xid jumped to ~0.3 (likely a batch of flaky cards).

cheng: Let's model spare pool as a simple hedging formula: N_spares = ceil(G * p * t * m)
where G = GPUs in region, p = failure prob/month, t = replacement lead time (months), m = correlated-failure multiplier.
Plugging conservative numbers: G=4000 (us-west-2), p=0.012 (1.2%), t=0.25 (1 week ≈ 0.25 mo), m=2 -> N = ceil(4000*0.012*0.25*2) = ceil(24) = 24.
This covers typical failures plus possible correlated batch events.

sam: Cost estimate check: reserved spare node ≈ $2.4k/mo (gpu + infra). 24 spares = ~$57.6k/mo. If we keep fewer spares, risk incurring incident costs. Example back-of-envelope: 3 incidents/yr * 2hr avg * 1% revenue impact ≈ $120k/yr loss. So 16 spares (~$38.4k/mo) might still be cheaper than repeated outages depending on SLA penalties.

leo: For operationalization, propose drain rules and automation:
- auto-drain if corrected ECC > 50 in 24h OR Xid fatal > 3 within 1h OR uncorrected ECC > 1.
- on drain: create hw-replace ticket, mark node state=decommissioning, attach serial and AZ, and move workloads to reserve pool.
Command example:
```bash
hwctl drain --node $NODE --reason "ecc:53/24h" --ticket create
fleetctl set-state $NODE decommissioning --meta "replace_ticket=$TICKET"
```

maria: +1. Also suggest baseline hedging per 1000 GPUs so smaller regions don't starve: baseline_spares_per_1000 = 3. Scaling rule suggestion: baseline + ceil((G/1000) * max(3, round(p*100))). For G=4k, p=0.012 -> baseline 3 + ceil(4 * max(3, 1)) = 3 + 12 = 15 (we'd still apply multiplier for correlated events to get to ~30 for worst-case).

ach: (typo, meant aj) I'll run Monte Carlo on Friday to give probability curves across 6/12 month horizons — will commit a notebook to the infra-runbooks repo.

ops-bot: incident-bot: created INC-2026-341 for us-west-2 gpu error spike — https://redwood/ops/incidents/INC-2026-341 :rotating_light:

cheng: Notes for runbook update:
- replacement lead time assumptions: on-site swap = 1w, hotspare reprovision = 2h. Use whichever is the longer for regional planning.
- keep hotspares AZ-local where latency matters; cross-AZ fallback only for non-latency-critical tiers.
- weekly recalculation: run job that pulls last 30d p, computes N_spares and flags if current reserve < target.

maria: Action items: @aj run the sim Friday, @cheng update capacity playbook with the formula and thresholds, @leo add automation hooks for hwctl drain and ticket creation. We'll target a temporary reserve of 20 for us-west-2 while we finish sims.

sam: sounds good. If sims show heavy tail risk, recommend budgeting for extra 8-12 spares for seasonal peaks.

maria: thanks — I'll post the sim results and put a short note in the capacity-runbook.
